summary: Introduces the two reporting servers AAPS can upload to, Nightscout (recommended, near real time, allows remote commands) and Tidepool (reports only, three-hour delay), and the self-hosted or paid hosting options for Nightscout. It is a planning page; app settings are covered on the Nightscout and Tidepool pages.

sections.heading: Setting up the Reporting Server
sections.summary: Page title and intro: Nightscout and Tidepool are the two reporting servers; Nightscout is recommended.

sections.heading: Nightscout
sections.summary: What Nightscout does for AAPS users and caregivers: near-real-time data, reports and remote commands.

sections.heading: Option 1 - Set up your Nightscout server yourself
sections.summary: Self-hosting Nightscout, with the maintenance and migration effort it may need.

sections.heading: Option 2 - Pay for a hosted Nightscout service
sections.summary: Paying a provider to host Nightscout, with a link to a vendor comparison.

sections.heading: Further configuration of Nightscout
sections.summary: Pointer to the Nightscout configuration page.

sections.heading: Tidepool
sections.summary: Tidepool as a free reporting-only option suited to sharing reports with the clinic; AAPS uploads to it directly, so the separate Tidepool uploader must not be used.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.summary: Continue with a dedicated Google account or with building the AAPS app.
